title: How Can ChatGPT Facilitate Teaching and Learning: Implications for Contemporary Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the emerging question of how ChatGPT and similar generative AI tools may affect teaching and learning in contemporary education. Rather than testing an intervention empirically, it offers an argumentative review of the literature and a conceptual discussion of opportunities, risks, and policy implications associated with ChatGPT in schools and higher education.

The article focuses on ChatGPT as both a student aide and a teacher aide. For students, it highlights personalized tutoring, instant feedback, language support, problem-solving help, and assistance for learners with disabilities or learning difficulties. For teachers, it argues that ChatGPT can support lesson planning, content generation, presentation design, creation of assessment items and rubrics, grading assistance, and provision of instructional ideas. The paper also emphasizes that these uses should be guided by human oversight and ethical awareness.

No specific participant sample, intervention implementation, or setting is reported because the paper is not an empirical study. Its main conclusion is that ChatGPT has substantial potential to augment teaching and learning, but realizing these benefits depends on responsible use, digital leadership, policy support, and teacher preparation. The authors frame ChatGPT as a technology that can enrich pedagogy and reduce workload while still requiring careful management of its pitfalls.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model chatbot for generating and refining text, answering questions, and providing interactive assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses ChatGPT as a generative AI tool that can help teachers with lesson planning, instructional support, presentation development, customized materials, and assessment/feedback tasks.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an argumentative review paper rather than an empirical study. It summarizes potential uses of ChatGPT in education but does not report original data, study design, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues that ChatGPT may be useful for lesson planning, instructional support, and feedback, but it provides no effect sizes or empirical outcome data. Impact therefore cannot be estimated from the article itself and remains unclear.
